title: Reasoning routine for a new accounting scenario
summary: Use a stable question order before proposing accounts or code. This prevents an LLM from confusing legal entity, establishment, tax registration, regulator, client-money perimeter, reporting boundary and operational source authority.
invariants: Do not start with debit/credit lines; first establish whose books, what happened, and which authority proves it.
Do not infer tax jurisdiction from company domicile, regulatory scope from tax scope, establishment from legal entity, or consolidation from a cross-entity report.
Do not invent an accounting treatment when legal/economic substance is unresolved; carry evidence and defer the treatment to the effective policy.
Do not manufacture a subsidiary merely because one legal entity has an overseas place of business, tax registration or regulator relationship.
procedure: 1. Name the legal entity whose AccountingBook may change.
2. Identify the authoritative operational/economic event, sourceEventRef, source authority and immutable evidence.
3. Identify the effective accounting policy generation and exact executable policy identity for that entity/event/date.
4. Identify orthogonal scopes: establishment, tax registration/election, regulator, client-money arrangement, matter, counterparty and relationship kind.
5. If tax is involved, determine tax under the selected registration/election/ruleset before accounting the result.
6. If settlement rounding is involved, apply its separate election only after the accounted obligation exists; never let it rewrite tax.
7. Post exact whole minor-unit journal lines, balanced independently by currency.
8. For external filings, import into an assessment book rather than native GL truth.
9. For reports, select immutable journal evidence through a ReportingBoundary; do not repost the ledger to make a report.
10. For corrections, create new journals/snapshots/filings and explicit lineage; never rewrite historical evidence.

provenance.claim: Architecture separates legal entity, event/policy/posting, scopes, tax, settlement, assessment and reporting evidence.
Preferred reasoning begins from authoritative operational evidence and exact legal-entity accounting policy, not from invented journal lines.
